papers.title_en: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
papers.authors: Jiajie Zhang, Yankai Xiang, Changhao Chen
papers.evidence: 在智能体规划器下组合冻结VLA技能并解决技能衔接问题
papers.tldr: 冻结VLA技能在长程组合的接缝处常因刚性复现轨迹而碰撞场景残留，即使重新归位也难避免。作者提出Skill Envelope：用成功执行轨迹测出技能的3D几何包络，并以CHECK检测阻挡物、FREE寻找安全放置区，让VLA负责分布内操作、代码修复分布外状态。在LIBERO-Goal上碰撞预测AUROC达0.946，接缝准备度0.902超过前沿VLM，两步与三四步任务成功率显著提升。结果表明可靠组合应测量策略物理工作空间，而非用语言猜测前置条件。
papers.abstract_en: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $π_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

papers.title_en: Atomic Policy: Composing Atomic Manipulation Skills with Agentic Reasoning
papers.authors: Kaidi Zhang, Pengyuan Guo, Zhengtong Xu, Caiyi Zhang, Huayi Gou, Guanlin Huang, Aaron Lim, Anas Rafei, Yu She
papers.evidence: VLM估计符号状态与目标，PDDL求解器规划技能并由智能体框架调用与验证
papers.tldr: 长程操作要求机器人在动态场景中把任务意图转化为物理交互，但VLM语义推理与视觉运动策略控制难以直接衔接，且目标模糊、动作依赖复杂。Atomic Policy用VLM估计符号状态与目标，由PDDL求解器生成技能计划，并通过语言、视觉指向或二者结合来引导和校验每个原子技能。仿真与真机实验显示，该方法提升任务遵循能力，并能在复杂长程操作中支持失败恢复与重规划。其贡献在于以相位级通用接口组合专用策略与通用动作模型。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to translate task intent into physical interactions as the scene changes. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer semantic and spatial reasoning, while visuomotor policies provide fine-grained control. Yet ambiguous goals and dependencies between actions make their integration challenging. We introduce Atomic Policy, a framework that composes learned manipulation skills through grounded steering and execution feedback. A VLM estimates the symbolic state and goal, and a PDDL solver constructs a skill plan. An agentic harness steers each skill through language, visual pointing, or both, and verifies its outcome to guide phase transitions and replanning. A common phase-level interface supports specialized policies and generalist action models. Experiments in simulation and on a real robot show how Atomic Policy improves task following and supports recovery in complex, long-horizon manipulation. Project page: https://aaronzkd.github.io/atomic-policy/

papers.title_en: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Liyang Li, Mingyu Liu, Xiaoman Li, Zhiyue Zhao, Jin-Chuan Shi, Canyu Zhao, Haokai Zhang, Jinyuan Tian, Linhao Zhong, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen
papers.evidence: 视觉语言模型作为高层控制器，通过工具调用完成机器人操作
papers.tldr: 紧凑开源VLM在机器人操作中仍难媲美前沿模型。RoboHarness-RL先监督微调教师示范，再用任务结果奖励做多轮强化学习，并借LiteHarness分层记忆压缩交互上下文。Qwen3.5-9B成功率在RoboTwin 2.0由31.2%升至44.0%，LIBERO-Pro由57.8%升至73.3%，随机场景亦提升。该框架无需VLA或世界动作模型，提升工具调用式机器人操作效率与鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic harnesses enable frontier vision-language models (VLMs) to manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tools, yet achieving comparable performance with compact open-weight VLMs remains challenging. We present RoboHarness-RL, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for improving VLM-based robot manipulation through tool calls. Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, the VLM further improves through multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, without relying on vision-language-action models or world action models. To support efficient multi-turn training, we develop LiteHarness, which uses hierarchical memory to keep interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; these gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis further shows that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to $4\times$, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/RoboHarness-RL/

papers.title_en: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents
papers.authors: Jinhao Zhang, Yushen Zuo, Ke Rui, Weitao Zhou, Haibao Yu, Honglong Tian, Xiaoheng Ma, Jie Mei, Jiawei Wang, Minglei Li
papers.evidence: 联合训练VLM与世界动作模型，融合语义规划与动作控制
papers.tldr: 现有世界动作模型虽能预测物理动态与动作分布，却缺乏开放世界语义理解和长程规划能力；视觉语言模型具备语义先验但难以有效融入控制。CoT-WAM通过可学习嵌入在VLM与WAM间交换信息，并用文本与目标图像监督该嵌入，配合两阶段联合训练实现协同。它在LIBERO、CALVIN、RoboCasa-Kitchen达到SOTA，在LIBERO-Plus/Pro零样本泛化更强，并提升RoboCasa365长程规划，真实实验验证有效。
papers.abstract_en: General robot manipulation requires both semantic competence and physical foresight. World action models (WAMs) acquire an understanding of and predictive capability over the physical world by jointly modeling visual foresight and action distributions. However, existing WAMs still lack semantic competence: they have limited ability to perform open-world scene understanding, semantic reasoning, and long-horizon planning. Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide these capabilities, effectively integrating their semantic priors into WAM prediction and control remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose CoT-WAM, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework. CoT-WAM uses a learnable embedding to exchange information between the VLM and the WAM, which is supervised by textual and goal-image signals during training to encode rich intent information. A tailored two-stage training strategy enables joint optimization and more effective collaboration between the VLM and WAM. We evaluate CoT-WAM on six benchmarks covering control performance, zero-shot generalization, and long-horizon planning. CoT-WAM achieves SOTA performance on LIBERO, CALVIN, and RoboCasa-Kitchen, and demonstrates stronger zero-shot generalization on LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-Pro without fine-tuning. On RoboCasa365, it further improves long-horizon planning over baselines with and without external planners. Real-world experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in practical deployments. Code is available at: https://github.com/jhz1192/CoT-WAM.git

papers.title_en: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
papers.authors: Yuhang Huang, Junchao Li, Boyang Ma, Minghui Xu, Kaidi Xu, Pengfei Hu, Xiuzhen Cheng, Yue Zhang
papers.evidence: 大模型解读用户意图并协调机器人动作模型，研究语义错位
papers.tldr: 商用机器人依赖大语言模型理解用户意图，并由机器人专用动作模型生成执行命令，但理解、模型协作与物理运动之间存在语义边界，可能使用户输入不含显式动作指令时仍触发非预期动作。为测量该风险，本文提出黑盒框架TARS，系统探索命令-推理-动作流水线，自动发现并验证非预期物理行为。在四款商用机器人、44种设置、133400次执行中，TARS发现普遍的跨模型动作错位，验证动作覆盖率达94%。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied robots increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction. This multi-model pipeline creates a critical semantic boundary across mind, model collaboration, and motion: semantic consistency may break between what the large model understands, how the small action model translates that understanding into executable commands, and what physical actions the robot ultimately performs. As a security consequence, commercial robots may execute unintended physical actions even when user inputs contain no explicit action commands. To measure this problem, we develop TARS, a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors. We evaluate TARS on four commercial robots across 44 experimental settings, conducting 133,400 executions. TARS uncovers widespread cross-model action misalignment and achieves up to 94% verified action coverage.

papers.title_en: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
papers.authors: Jiachen Tao, Gengyu Zhang, Haoxuan Wang, Bing Liu, Yan Yan
papers.evidence: 冻结VLM用语言指出下一步原子技能来指导策略，不直接输出动作
papers.tldr: 通用机器人策略能可靠执行原子技能，却在长程组合任务中失效；仅靠自身经验自我提升会困在原分布。CoachSI用冻结的现成VLM充当语言教练，观看机器人并只输出下一步原子指令，不输出动作；成功轨迹经事后重标注后微调策略。在基线停滞状态上，子目标完成率提升4.6倍；微调后未见场景长程任务无辅助成功率从47.4%升至59.3%，高于人类示范与自采集成功微调。该方法表明语言教练可让冻结动作骨干学会下一步该做什么，再由已有技能完成执行。
papers.abstract_en: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own. On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees. After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines. The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.

papers.title_en: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
papers.authors: Wei Dai, Jinkun Liu, Jiayi Chen, Han Liu, Wenbo Ding, Shaolun Huang
papers.evidence: 视觉语言模型通过工具接口编写并执行控制代码充当闭环机器人控制器
papers.tldr: 开放权重VLM作为机器人智能体时，常因工具契约失败、黑盒教师不可蒸馏、纯模仿学习分布漂移而表现不佳。EmbodyAgent用黑盒轨迹合成、SFT蒸馏和在线RL三段式后训练，共享无原语Python执行工具。在LIBERO Spatial上，留出成功率从0/100升至SFT 14/100、RL 84/100，训练rollout成功率8.4%升至87.7%。该工作给出端到端可执行代码智能体后训练范式，并揭示和缓解结果型RL诱发的运行时错误模式。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

papers.title_en: EmboEagle: An Efficient Agentic Embodied Framework for Long-horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Fan Xu, Zhongtao Wang, Hao Wu, Yitong Zhu, Wenzhuo Ma, Long Li, Zhuohao Li, Zhisheng Chen, Rui Su, Kun Wang, Xian Wu, Wanli Ouyang
papers.evidence: 以子任务为条件控制并结合视觉语言模型监督的智能体长程操作框架
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作需跨阶段可靠执行，但独立世界-动作模型易累积物理误差，而无状态VLM监督延迟高且缺乏三维空间持续性。EmboEagle以闭环智能体框架统一子任务条件WAM控制、潜空间自适应监督与记忆引导几何恢复。它在RMBench和LIBERO-Mem达91.3%与90.6%成功率，分别超最强基线8.0和9.8个百分点，并将VLM调用较逐块监控降低74.2%。该工作提升了长程操作的成功率与推理效率。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon robotic manipulation demands reliable execution across interdependent stages, yet standalone World-Action Models (WAMs) suffer from compounding physical errors, while stateless Vision-Language Model (VLM) supervision incurs prohibitive chunkwise latency and lacks 3D spatial persistence. We present EmboEagle, a closed-loop agentic framework that unifies subtask-conditioned WAM control, latent-space adaptive supervision, and memory-guided geometric recovery. First, we adapt sequential WAMs via decoupled two-stage flow matching that preserves cross-stage visual history while calibrating truncated action supervision at subtask boundaries. Second, without an auxiliary vision encoder, we distill teacher intervention decisions into a lightweight routing gate driven solely by the WAM Action Expert's pre- and post-chunk latent transitions and subtask embeddings. Third, upon invocation, the VLM decouples diagnostic status from discrete routing actions and executes parameterized recovery primitives grounded in structured memory (initial references, active grasp bindings, and tool traces), followed by mandatory post-repair verification. Across RMBench and LIBERO-Mem, EmboEagle achieves 91.3\% and 90.6\% average success, surpassing the strongest baselines by 8.0 and 9.8 percentage points, while boosting real-world success over VoLoAgent under identical executor weights. Moreover, adaptive gating cuts VLM calls by 74.2\% versus chunkwise monitoring (91.3\% vs. 93.7\% success).

papers.title_en: Ground, Guide, Act: Improving VLA Spatial Generalization with Multimodal Foundation Models
papers.authors: Guangting Zheng, Shaoxuan Wang, Yu Yuan, Zhipeng Tang, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang
papers.evidence: 多模态基础模型负责定位与引导，VLA负责执行
papers.tldr: VLA模型能从示教中学习动作策略，却难以泛化到物体位置变化与新任务目标，而通用多模态基础模型虽具备空间理解能力，却难以直接用于细粒度控制。作者通过原子阶段干预分析发现，失败主要源于目标定位与全局空间路由不佳，局部操作技能本身仍可用。为此提出MFM-VLA选择性协作框架：由多模态基础模型负责目标定位与空间引导，控制器执行自由空间运动，VLA保留精细操作，并用动作块级几何描述与扰动恢复数据微调。在LIBERO-PRO等四个基准及真实化学任务上，成功率分别提升14.9、74.0、3.6和30.9个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models effectively learn action policies from robot demonstrations, but struggle to generalize to changes in object positions and task goals. General multimodal foundation models (MFMs) offer complementary scene understanding and spatial reasoning, but remain slow and unreliable for direct fine-grained control. To understand how MFMs can improve VLA spatial generalization, we conduct a systematic capability analysis across multiple VLA architectures using atomic-stage interventions, revealing that many failures stem from poor target grounding and global spatial routing, while local manipulation skills remain largely usable. Based on these findings, we propose MFM-VLA, a selective collaboration framework in which an MFM provides target grounding and spatial guidance, controllers execute free-space motion, and the VLA retains control over fine-grained manipulation. We fine-tune the VLA with action-chunk-level dense geometric captions and perturbed-state recovery data to improve local guidance following and recovery from unfamiliar handoff states. A development-calibrated capability router selects between direct VLA execution and MFM-assisted execution to avoid unnecessary intervention. Across LIBERO-PRO, ALOHA-Sim-PRO, RoboCasa365, and real-world chemistry tasks, MFM-VLA improves success rates by 14.9, 74.0, 3.6, and 30.9 percentage points, respectively, over the corresponding base VLA. The project page is available at https://tom-zgt.github.io/MFM-VLA

papers.title_en: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
papers.authors: Daehee Lee, Dongsu Lee, Sanghyun Ahn, Minjong Yoo, Honguk Woo
papers.evidence: 依据高层任务规范重构可复用过程知识以组合技能
papers.tldr: 通用行为模型在训练中已内化大量程序性知识，适应新目标与技能接口更多是重组已有能力而非从零学习。论文将这一能力定义为可重构性，并提出 RecPo 框架，用多视图任务无关地表征技能，在部署时通过同一组视图解析任务规格，并在存储的技能转移关系上求解组合查询以绑定技能执行。在扩展 Franka Kitchen 长程任务上，RecPo 取得 91.9% 的有序完成率，每回合任务推理仅需 1.0 ms，并在真机上通过局部记忆编辑实现免重训练的适应。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes. RecPo maintains a procedure knowledge base of skill-induced transitions, with each view exposing a reusable factor and preserving local skill connectivity. At deployment, it interprets task specifications through the same views and resolves the resulting compositional queries over the stored relations to bind skills for execution. On long-horizon tasks in an extended Franka Kitchen benchmark, RecPo achieves 91.9% ordered completion with 1.0 ms of task inference per episode across varying procedure support and task-record sparsity. Real-robot studies further demonstrate adaptation through local memory edits without task-specific retraining.

papers.title_en: CoBoVLA: Decoupling Language from Action with Discrete Codes for Robust and Interpretable Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Mehul Arora, Dhruv Agarwal, Ambuj Agrawal
papers.evidence: 在VLA内解耦语言理解、规划与控制
papers.tldr: 现有VLA在LIBERO上成功率高，但对指令改写敏感，且语言理解与动作生成耦合导致失败难定位。CoBoVLA用2.5亿参数，将语言理解、规划与控制经离散可解释码解耦：文本编码器生成共享步骤码，视觉规划器转为动作码序列，由语言无关执行器执行。它在LIBERO-Goal达91.4%，优于SmolVLA的82.8%，控制延迟17毫秒；在LIBERO-Para的4092条未见改写上达81.1%。该设计提升改写鲁棒性并支持分阶段诊断。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models achieve high success rates on the LIBERO benchmark but remain sensitive to paraphrasing. Existing VLAs ranging from 0.6B to 7.5B parameters experience a 22-52 point performance drop on LIBERO-Para while SmolVLA exhibits an even larger decline, from 83\% to 8\%. Because most VLAs jointly learn language understanding and action generation, it is difficult to determine whether a failure originates from misunderstanding an instruction or executing it incorrectly. To address these challenges, we introduce CoBoVLA, or CodeBookVLA, a 250M-parameter VLA that decouples language understanding, planning, and control through learned discrete interpretable codes. A text encoder maps the instructions to shared step codes, which a visual planner then converts into action code sequences executed by a language-independent actor. This design improves robustness to instruction paraphrasing while allowing failures to be traced to individual stages. It also enables efficient real-time control on resource-constrained hardware by encoding instructions only once and using compact discrete representations to keep each component lightweight. CoBoVLA achieves 91.4\% success on LIBERO-Goal, compared with 82.8\% for SmolVLA, under a matched protocol, with 17 ms per control step latency. On LIBERO-Para, it achieves 81.1\% across 4,092 unseen paraphrases and 78.5\% on matched episodes, compared with 36.5\% for SmolVLA LoRA fine-tuned on paraphrases. Without two-step demonstrations, CoBoVLA completes 48.8\% of 160 free-form two-step tasks. Finally, success reaches 91\% when instructions are correctly encoded but falls to 27.2\% otherwise, identifying language understanding as the main source of remaining failures. Together, these results demonstrate that decoupling language understanding and control can improve instruction robustness while making VLA failures easier to diagnose.

papers.title_en: Verify2Act: Critic-Guided Latent World Models for Verifying Language-Conditioned Manipulation Plans
papers.evidence: VLM提出多步操作计划并由潜世界模型验证
papers.tldr: 针对VLM多步操作计划缺乏场景变化接地、像素级世界模型慢且长程漂移的问题，Verify2Act将语义动作提议与潜在物理验证解耦。VLM提出候选计划，V2A-WM在DINOv2特征空间想象执行，双头critic执行前检查时序一致性与目标满足。系统仅用数字孪生数据训练并部署于低成本机械臂，六类语言条件任务成功率达83.3%，显著优于单独VLM与像素扩散世界模型。该框架实现执行前验证且无规划导致失败，为语言条件操作计划提供高效可靠的潜在世界模型验证方案。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. We deploy the full system on a low-cost robot arm, training the world model and critic only on data generated in a digital twin. Across six language-conditioned tasks, Verify2Act reaches 83.3\% task success, compared with 61.7\% for a latent world model without our architectural changes, 53.3\% for the VLM alone, and 46.7\% for a pixel-diffusion world model. It verified every plan it executed and incurred no planning-induced failures: all of its failed episodes were caused by low-level grasp or placement slips. In simulation, Verify2Act obtains the highest five-task chain success on CALVIN among the compared baselines with 30$\times$ fewer reflective VLM calls than pixel-diffusion verification, and the highest success on cluttered nut assembly.

papers.title_en: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Kai Lu, Chenyang Ma, Ioannis Havoutis
papers.evidence: 用状态机将长程任务分解为分阶段技能执行
papers.tldr: 长时程人形移动操作要求时序、技能与精度紧耦合，单体VLA难以稳定完成。PGX将时序与精度控制卸载到两个免训练组件，使VLA专注阶段特定技能。它用物理谓词状态机门控阶段转换与恢复，并用世界坐标锁定保持基站、物体与接触目标一致。在三个仿真任务和Unitree G1真实世界任务上，阶段推进与成功率均提升，为长时程人形操作提供可扩展方案。
papers.abstract_en: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

papers.title_en: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Meng-Hao Guo, Yi Zhang, Zhe-Han Mo, Han-Zheng Wang, Jia-Jun Wang, Xin-Sheng Chen, Jiaxi Song, Yi-Xuan Deng, Jia-Ning Li, Xuanyu Chu, Hengrui Zhang, Huan-ang Gao, Yongming Rao, Shi-Min Hu
papers.evidence: 将视觉语言模型训练为操作基础模型并使用语义动作原语
papers.tldr: 针对GPT-6 Astra机器人控制能力训练细节未公开、难以复现的问题，nanoAstra把机器人行为建模为由可复用参数化动作原语组成的语义步骤，并以显式进度描述引导，同时用CP-SFT将输出约束到结构化动作空间。模型在超过5000小时机器人数据与通用VQA数据上联合训练，在RoboTwin 2.0随机基准上取得17.8%零样本成功率。其推理速度快于单张H20上的动作执行，可流式重叠推理与运动，把机器人空闲时间从35.0%大幅降至6.9%。
papers.abstract_en: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities. With this formulation, we train nanoAstra on more than 5,000 hours of robot data together with general VQA data. On RoboTwin 2.0's randomized benchmark, nanoAstra-9B achieves a 17.8% zero-shot success rate, substantially outperforming advanced VLA and WAM baselines as well as similarly sized VLMs. With inference faster than the corresponding motion execution on a single H20 GPU, our model supports action-chunk-like streaming execution that overlaps inference with motion, reducing the robot's idle time from 35.0% to 6.9%.
